proof:
Source: Steps 3(a), 3(c), 5 and 8(a)–(c) of the selected node's supplied proof (F3–F4 of the cone-filling proof; Simon Ch. 6, 2.30 and 3.10, book/chapter-06.txt lines 528–551 and 857–865), specialized to one piece.
CF(a), CF(b), CF(c) denote parts (a), (b), (c) of the sibling cylinder_fubini, i.e. the reused accepted lemma cmcdt_lpi_cyl_fubini applied with n := k and this Borel set A. Its cylinder is exactly Cyl(A), and its ι(t, u) is WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)).

Proof.
1. (τ and ι.) τ is linear in finitely many coordinates, hence continuous and Borel measurable. For t ∈ ℝ and u ∈ ℝ^k, τ(ι(t, u)) = u and (WithLp.ofLp ι(t, u)) 0 = t (WithLp.ofLp_toLp, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_zero, WithLp.toLp_ofLp).
2. (Part (a).) g and τ are measurable, so g ∘ τ is measurable (Measurable.comp). The coercion ℤ → ℝ is measurable (ℤ has the discrete σ-algebra).
   Hence z ↦ (g(τ z) : ℝ) is measurable, and so is the [0, ∞]-valued z ↦ ‖(g(τ z) : ℝ)‖ₑ.
3. (Part (b).) By CF(b) with f(z) := ‖(g(τ z) : ℝ)‖ₑ and step 1,
   ∫⁻_{Cyl(A)} ‖g(τ z)‖ₑ dz = ∫⁻_{u∈A} ∫⁻_{t∈(0,1)} ‖g(u)‖ₑ dt du = ∫⁻_{u∈A} ‖g(u)‖ₑ·λ((0,1)) du = ∫⁻_A ‖g(u)‖ₑ du.
   Here the inner integrand is constant in t (setLIntegral_const) and λ((0,1)) = ofReal(1 − 0) = 1 (Real.volume_Ioo).
   The last integral is finite because (g : ℝ) is integrable on A.
   z ↦ (g(τ z) : ℝ) is measurable (step 2), so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to Cyl(A). With the finite integral above, it is integrable on Cyl(A).
4. (Bounds.) ω is continuous with compact support, so there is M with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M for all y ∈ ℝ^P (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous; operator norm of the continuous alternating map ω(y)). Necessarily M ≥ 0.
   G is K-Lipschitz for some K ≥ 0, so ‖DG(z)‖ ≤ K for every z (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
   Hence ‖DG(z)e_a‖ ≤ ‖DG(z)‖·‖e_a‖ = ‖DG(z)‖ ≤ K for every z and every index a, as ‖e_a‖ = 1.
5. (Measurability of the integrand.) Put Φ(z) := (g(τ z) : ℝ)·ω(G z)(∂G(z)).
   z ↦ DG(z) is Borel measurable (measurable_fderiv), so each z ↦ DG(z)e_a is measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const), and z ↦ ∂G(z) ∈ (ℝ^P)^{k+1} is measurable (measurable_pi_iff).
   G is continuous, so z ↦ (G(z), ∂G(z)) ∈ ℝ^P × (ℝ^P)^{k+1} is measurable (Measurable.prodMk).
   The map Ψ(y, v) := ω(y)(v) on ℝ^P × (ℝ^P)^{k+1} is continuous: ω is continuous, and evaluation of continuous alternating maps is jointly continuous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.instContinuousEval, Continuous.eval).
   So Ψ is Borel measurable, and z ↦ ω(G z)(∂G(z)) = Ψ(G z, ∂G z) is measurable. With step 2, Φ is measurable.
6. (Integrability of Φ.) For every z, |ω(G z)(∂G(z))| ≤ ‖ω(G z)‖·∏_{a=0}^{k} ‖DG(z)e_a‖ ≤ M·K^{k+1} (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and step 4).
   So |Φ(z)| ≤ M K^{k+1}·|g(τ z)|. The right-hand side is integrable on Cyl(A) by part (b) (Integrable.const_mul), and Φ is measurable (step 5).
   Hence Φ is integrable on Cyl(A) (Integrable.mono').
7. (Fubini.) By CF(c) applied to Φ, which is integrable on Cyl(A) by step 6:
   ∫_{Cyl(A)} Φ = ∫_{u∈A} ∫_{t∈(0,1)} Φ(ι(t, u)) dt du.
8. (Integrand on the cylinder; multilinearity.) Fix u ∈ A and t ∈ (0, 1). By step 1 and the hypotheses, g(τ(ι(t, u))) = g(u), G(ι(t, u)) = t·F(u) and ∂G(ι(t, u)) = Fin.cons (F u) (t·∂F(u)).
   Let c := Fin.cons 1 (fun _ => t) ∈ ℝ^{k+1} and v := Fin.cons (F u) (∂F(u)). Then Fin.cons (F u) (t·∂F(u)) = (c_a·v_a)_a: at a = 0 both sides are 1·F(u), and at a = b+1 both are t·DF(u)e'_b.
   ω(y) is multilinear, so ω(y)((c_a v_a)_a) = (∏_a c_a)·ω(y)(v) = t^k·ω(y)(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ; ∏_a c_a = 1·t^k by Fin.prod_univ_succ and Finset.prod_const).
   Hence Φ(ι(t, u)) = g(u)·(t^k·ω(t·F(u))(Fin.cons (F u) (∂F(u)))).
9. (Inner integral.) Fix u ∈ A. By step 8 the two integrands below agree on (0, 1) (setIntegral_congr_fun with measurableSet_Ioo), and g(u) is a constant factor (integral_const_mul):
   ∫_{t∈(0,1)} Φ(ι(t, u)) dt = ∫_{(0,1)} g(u)·(t^k ω(tF(u))(Fin.cons (F u) (∂F u))) dt = g(u)·∫_{(0,1)} t^k ω(tF(u))(Fin.cons (F u) (∂F u)) dt.
   Moreover ∫_{(0,1)} h = ∫_{(0,1]} h = ∫_0^1 h for every h: λ has no atoms (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo), and intervalIntegral.integral_of_le applies with 0 ≤ 1.
10. (Outer integral.) A is measurable, and by step 9 the two functions of u agree on A. By setIntegral_congr_fun,
   ∫_A ∫_{(0,1)} Φ(ι(t, u)) dt du = ∫_A g(u)·(∫_0^1 t^k ω(tF(u))(Fin.cons (F u) (∂F u)) dt) du.
   Together with step 7 this is (c).
Steps 2, 3 and 10 prove (a), (b) and (c). ∎

example (k P : ℕ) (G : Euclid (k+1) → Euclid P) (hG : Continuous G) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k+1)) (hω : Continuous ω) :
    Measurable (fun z => ω (G z) (fun a => fderiv ℝ G z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) := by
  have h1 : Measurable (fun z => (G z, fun a : Fin (k+1) => fderiv ℝ G z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) := by
    refine hG.measurable.prodMk ?_
    exact measurable_pi_iff.mpr (fun a => measurable_fderiv_apply_const ℝ G (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))
  have h2 : Continuous (fun p : Euclid P × (Fin (k+1) → Euclid P) => ω p.1 p.2) :=
    (hω.comp continuous_fst).eval continuous_snd
  exact h2.measurable.comp h1
key_steps: g∘τ is measurable. By Tonelli on the cylinder (cylinder_fubini (b)), ∫⁻_{Cyl A}|g∘τ| = ∫⁻_A |g| < ∞, so g∘τ is integrable on Cyl A.
Φ(z) = g(τz)·ω(Gz)(∂Gz) is measurable: (y, v) ↦ ω(y)(v) is continuous, G is continuous and fderiv is Borel. Also |Φ| ≤ sup‖ω‖·K^{k+1}·|g∘τ|, so Φ is integrable on Cyl A.
Fubini on the cylinder (cylinder_fubini (c)) gives ∫_{Cyl A} Φ = ∫_A ∫_{(0,1)} Φ(ι(t,u)) dt du.
On the cylinder Φ(ι(t,u)) = g(u)·t^k·ω(tF(u))(Fin.cons (F u) (∂F u)), by the hypotheses and multilinearity in the last k slots. Pulling out g(u) and identifying ∫_{(0,1)} with ∫_0^1 gives (c).
